examples: Spring came so it is warm.
nuance: 봄 is the spring season from March to May and is known for warm weather and blooming flowers like cherry blossoms.
mistakes: Saying 봄에서 instead of 봄에 for when something happens

examples: I go to the sea in summer.
In summer it rains a lot.
nuance: 여름 is the summer season from June to August and is hot and humid, with a rainy period called 장마 in the middle.
mistakes: Confusing 여름 summer with 겨울 winter when describing weather

examples: Autumn leaves are pretty in autumn.
Autumn came so it is cool.
nuance: 가을 is the autumn season from September to November and is famous for cool air and colorful fall foliage called 단풍.
mistakes: Spelling it 가울 instead of the correct 가을

examples: In winter I wear warm clothes.
nuance: 겨울 is the winter season from December to February and is cold and dry with snow, the coldest of the four seasons.
mistakes: Saying 겨울에서 instead of 겨울에 for the time something happens

examples: When the season changes I buy clothes.
nuance: 계절 means season in general and Korea has four distinct ones, so people often say 한국은 사계절이 뚜렷해요.
mistakes: Using 시즌 the loanword when natural Korean uses 계절

nuance: 날짜 means a calendar date and to ask which day of the month you say 며칠이에요, using Sino numbers for the day.
mistakes: Confusing 날짜 date with 요일 day of the week

examples: I eat seaweed soup on my birthday.
I bought a friend birthday gift.
nuance: 생일 is a birthday and on it Koreans eat 미역국, seaweed soup, while 생신 is the honorific word for elders.
mistakes: Using 생일 for an elder instead of the honorific 생신

examples: I rest at home on a day off.
On holidays the shop is closed.
nuance: 휴일 means a day off from work or a public holiday, and 공휴일 specifically means an official national holiday.
mistakes: Mixing up 휴일 day off with 휴가 a vacation leave

examples: I meet family in the new year.
nuance: 새해 means the new year and the standard greeting is 새해 복 많이 받으세요, wishing someone much fortune.
mistakes: Saying just 새해 복 많이 without the verb 받으세요

examples: I eat rice cake soup on Lunar New Year.
Family gathers on Lunar New Year.
On Lunar New Year we wear hanbok.
nuance: 설날 is the Korean Lunar New Year when families gather, eat 떡국 rice cake soup, and bow to elders in a custom called 세배.
mistakes: Confusing 설날 Lunar New Year with 새해 the general new year

examples: I go to my hometown on Chuseok.
On Chuseok we watch the full moon.
nuance: 추석 is the Korean autumn harvest festival, often called Korean Thanksgiving, when families eat 송편 and honor their ancestors.
mistakes: Calling 추석 a new year holiday instead of a harvest festival
